method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: QUOTED from Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis' (Jul–Sep 2026), 20 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 ('This is an open access article under the CC BY license') (read at NCBI PMC efetch JATS <license> element for PMC13251756 (Europe PMC returned 503 on 2026-09-23)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14) 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis' (published 22 July 2026), 10 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13425172). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps the Brazilian consensus claims (S1, quoted) unchanged and adds the ASH 2026 AL amyloidosis diagnosis guideline (S2, PMC13425172, CC BY-NC-ND, paraphrased) for GRADE-rated testing, imaging and biopsy-site recommendations.

claims.claim: **AL amyloidosis comes from a small clonal plasma-cell (or B-cell) population making unstable light chains that deposit in organs, mainly the heart and kidneys.** Early diagnosis matters because organ damage becomes irreversible.
claims.source_text: Immunoglobulin light chain amyloidosis (AL) is characterized by the excessive production of abnormal and unstable antibody light chains by a proliferative plasma cell or B cell clone. In the systemic disease, light chains produced by clonal cells in the bone marrow accumulate in multiple organs, particularly in the heart and kidneys … Diagnosing and treating AL amyloidosis early is therefore critical to reduce or eliminate the light chain-producing plasma cell clone and halt organ damage
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It is rare (5.1–12.8 per million a year), with median age at diagnosis 64;** MGUS and myeloma carry a significant risk of progressing to AL. One-year mortality is 12%–30%, reflecting late diagnosis, and heart involvement drives prognosis.
claims.source_text: AL amyloidosis is a relatively rare condition, with a worldwide incidence of 5.1-12.8 cases per million population … Median age at diagnosis is 64 years with incidence increasing with age; however there is no established association with ethnicity or geography []. Pre-existing plasma cell dyscrasias, including MGUS and multiple myeloma, carry a significant risk of progression to AL amyloidosis … One-year mortality is high (12%-30%), reflecting the failure to diagnose prior to irreversible end organ damage [,]. Heart involvement is the major determinant of prognosis and mortality
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Diagnosis is typically late:** 50% of patients see five or more doctors, and time from symptoms to diagnosis runs from about six months to 2.7 years. Early symptoms (fatigue, dizziness, neurological symptoms, abdominal pain) are vague.
claims.source_text: Early symptoms of AL amyloidosis are vague (i.e., neurologic symptoms, fatigue, dizziness, abdominal pain) and may be misattributed by patients and HCPs to other, more common conditions or simply as part of aging … The median time from symptom onset to AL amyloidosis diagnosis is approximately six months to 2.7 years with 50% of patients visiting five or more physicians of different medical specialties before diagnosis
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspect AL amyloidosis in HFpEF, nephrotic-range proteinuria without diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, unexplained hepatomegaly or diarrhoea, especially when several organs are involved.** Macroglossia, periorbital purpura, submandibular swelling and the shoulder pad sign are specific but rare.
claims.source_text: Symptoms that should immediately raise suspicion of possible AL amyloidosis include the involvement of soft tissues with macroglossia, periorbital purpura, submandibular gland swelling, and the shoulder pad sign; however, these highly specific symptoms are rare and occur only in a subset of individuals … In the absence of more specific symptoms, physicians should suspect AL amyloidosis when patients present with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, nephrotic-range proteinuria in the absence of diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, unexplained hepatomegaly, and diarrhea, especially when multiple organ systems are involved
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In people with MGUS, monitor ALP, proteinuria and NT-proBNP regularly** to catch early organ involvement.
claims.source_text: Biomarkers, including alkaline phosphatase (ALP), proteinuria, and NT-proBNP, should be monitored regularly in patients with MGUS to detect early signs of organ involvement
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Four steps:** clinical suspicion; find a monoclonal light chain; tissue diagnosis; then type the amyloid.
claims.source_text: Patients are assessed for AL amyloidosis using a 4-step algorithm: 1) Screening for clinical suspicion of AL amyloidosis, 2) identification of monoclonal light chains, 3) tissue diagnosis, and 4) typing of tissue employing adequate technologies
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Look for the monoclonal light chain with three tests: serum immunofixation, urine immunofixation and the serum kappa/lambda ratio.** Electrophoresis is often negative because the clone is small (under 10% of marrow cells), so it is usually left out.
claims.source_text: The presence of plasma cell dyscrasia in patients with suspected AL amyloidosis is determined by the identification of monoclonal light chains by three tests: serum protein immunofixation, urinary immunofixation, and the serum kappa/lambda ratio [,]. Because the clonal plasma cell population in AL amyloidosis is often small ( < 10% of total bone marrow cells), protein electrophoresis is frequently negative and therefore usually omitted from the diagnostic algorithm
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm amyloid on biopsy with Congo red and apple-green birefringence under polarised light.** Start with fat pad, bone marrow or salivary gland; together fat and marrow give 89% sensitivity (endomyocardial biopsy 93.5%).
claims.source_text: This confirmation is based on the demonstration of amorphous tissue material that stains positive with Congo red and exhibits the characteristic apple-green birefringence under polarized light, a critical step to avoid both false-positive and false-negative interpretations in the routine practice … the combination of fat pad sampling and bone marrow biopsy yields a high sensitivity (89%). When performed individually, however, sensitivity is significantly lower (76.6% and 55.1%, respectively), whereas endomyocardial biopsy demonstrates a sensitivity of 93.5%
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Negative fat and marrow biopsies do not exclude AL:** about a 15% chance of disease remains, so biopsy an affected organ when suspicion is high.
claims.source_text: However, negative fat and bone marrow biopsies do not rule out AL amyloidosis; there is still an approximate 15% chance of disease and hence further biopsies of the appropriate organs are recommended … In individuals who are highly suspected of having AL amyloidosis and have an absence of amyloid deposits in peripheral tissues, biopsy of an affected organ should be prioritized
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Type the amyloid protein** with immunological methods or mass spectrometry once Congo red is positive. With no monoclonal protein and suspected cardiac amyloid, do bone-tracer scintigraphy for ATTR and DNA testing to separate hereditary from wild-type.
claims.source_text: Once amyloid deposits have been confirmed with Congo red testing, the type of amyloid protein must be identified in a tissue biopsy using more specific methods such as immunological techniques or mass spectrometry … In the absence of a monoclonal component, patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis should be tested for transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis using cardiac scintigraphy with bone-seeking tracers, notably 99mTc-diphosphono-propanodicarboxylic acid, 99mTc-pyrophosphate, and 99mTc-hydroxymethylene diphosphonate [,]. A DNA analysis is necessary to differentiate between hereditary and wild-type ATTR amyloidosis and to dismiss other rarer hereditary forms
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected cardiac amyloidosis: send serum and urine immunofixation plus a serum free light chain assay with ratio** (strong; moderate certainty). Any one abnormal result raises suspicion. The same panel of tests is suggested for unexplained proteinuria (conditional).
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Never rely on serum or urine protein electrophoresis alone to screen:** ASH requires electrophoresis and immunofixation of both serum and urine together with serum free light chains. Urine immunofixation can use a 24-hour collection or an early-morning random sample, but assessing renal involvement needs the 24-hour collection. Read free light chains cautiously in renal impairment or autoimmune disease.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Monoclonal protein found, cardiac biomarkers raised:** if the echocardiogram is non-diagnostic, add cardiac MRI (conditional); if the echocardiogram already fits amyloidosis, skip MRI and go straight to tissue biopsy without delay (conditional).
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use bone scintigraphy (PYP, DPD, HMDP) to diagnose AL cardiac amyloidosis** (strong). It is recommended for ATTR only when free light chains are normal and immunofixation shows no monoclonal protein; use SPECT, not planar images alone, and offer genetic counselling whatever the family history.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Where to biopsy first:** suspected cardiac AL, either fat pad plus marrow together or go directly to endomyocardial biopsy (favoured when hereditary ATTR is a risk); suspected renal AL, fat pad plus marrow before renal biopsy; neuropathy with a monoclonal gammopathy, fat pad plus marrow before nerve biopsy. All are conditional. Proceed to the organ biopsy if these are negative and suspicion stays high, or up front if another renal or nerve disease is suspected.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Do not do a marrow biopsy in isolation** from immunological assays and cardiac biomarkers, and do not hold other tests (including target-organ biopsy) while waiting for it. AL neuropathy closely resembles the far more common diabetic neuropathy.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Multi-organ disease: start with fat pad plus marrow if they can be done quickly, otherwise biopsy the symptomatic heart or kidney** (conditional). For suspected gut amyloid take larger, deeper biopsies that include submucosa. Pathology samples from the last 3 years can be retested for amyloid.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Once amyloid is seen on histology, subtype it promptly with a validated method,** and take fat-pad samples in a way that allows subtyping.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **In myeloma or smouldering myeloma, stain existing marrow biopsies with Congo red** (conditional); a positive stain prompts reassessment for systemic AL.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Proven AL without cardiac symptoms still needs hs-troponin, a natriuretic peptide (BNP or NT-proBNP) and cardiac imaging at diagnosis** (strong; low certainty). Cardiac MRI is more accurate than echocardiography but limited by cost and access.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel, Blood Advances 10(14), 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines on diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis', published 22 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425172/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Staging rests on cardiac biomarkers (troponin T and NT-proBNP or BNP).** The Mayo 2004 model and its European modification are most used; the European version better predicts early death, Mayo 2012 better predicts late survival. A renal staging system (eGFR and proteinuria) predicts dialysis risk.
claims.source_text: Cardiac biomarkers assessed in these models include levels of troponin T (TnT) and NT-proBNP or brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) … The Mayo 2004 model and its European modification rely on TnT and NT-proBNP levels to assign risk and are most widely used to determine patient management, while the Mayo 2012 and BU models incorporate dFLC and BNP, as additional markers of disease burden, respectively [,]. The European modification of Mayo 2004 more accurately predicts early death than Mayo 2012; the Mayo 2012 more accurately predicts late survival than Mayo 2004 … A renal staging system, in which renal involvement is assessed as the eGFR level and degree of proteinuria, helps predict the risk of progression to dialysis
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use cardiac biomarkers at every stage:** diagnosis, prognosis, follow-up and transplant assessment.
claims.source_text: Cardiac biomarker testing should be used at every stage, including diagnosis, prognostic evaluation, patient follow-up, and assessing suitability for transplantation
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The goal is a rapid, deep haematological remission.** Organs can keep recovering for up to two years after light chains fall, so if at least a very good partial response is reached, do not change treatment early just because organs have not yet responded.
claims.source_text: The main goal of treatment is to achieve a rapid and deep hematological remission by eliminating or reducing the amyloid-producing clonal cell population … recovery can continue to improve for up to two years after treatment, even when the amount of amyloid deposit remains unchanged [, ]. Given this, if an adequate hematological response (very good partial response or higher) is achieved, it is recommended to avoid premature therapeutic changes despite a lack of organ response within the first few months
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First line: daratumumab plus bortezomib, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone** (the ANDROMEDA regimen), which improved the speed and depth of response, overall survival and survival free of major organ deterioration. If daratumumab is unavailable, use bortezomib-cyclophosphamide-dexamethasone.
claims.source_text: The current standard of care for newly diagnosed AL amyloidosis is the quadruplet regimen consisting of daratumumab, bortezomib, cyclophosphamide, and dexamethasone … Results of the ANDROMEDA study show that adding daratumumab to the combination of bortezomib-cyclophosphamide-dexamethasone regimen further improved the speed and depth of hematological response, resulting in a clinically meaningful and significant improvement in overall survival and survival free from major organ deterioration … In cases where daratumumab is unavailable, the bortezomib-cyclophosphamide-dexamethasone should be used.
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Autologous transplant suits only a minority (around 20%):** younger patients with limited cardiac involvement, selected by EHA-ISA risk-adapted criteria. Not for advanced cardiac disease (especially Stage IIIb), refractory pleural effusions or orthostatic hypotension, active GI bleeding, or factor X deficiency with bleeding. Conditioning melphalan is 200 mg/m² or 140 mg/m² by age, heart, kidneys and condition.
claims.source_text: Due to the high risk of mortality, ASCT is generally restricted to younger individuals with limited cardiac involvement, although evidence is lacking for its superiority over chemotherapy alone [,]. Indeed, only a small proportion of patients (around 20%) with AL amyloidosis are eligible for ASCT … Patient selection for ASCT should ideally follow risk-adapted recommendations, such as the European Hematology Association-International Society of Amyloidosis (EHA-ISA) guidelines for stem cell transplantation in systemic AL amyloidosis []. ASCT should not be offered to patients with: advanced cardiac involvement (particularly Stage IIIb disease), medically refractory pleural effusions, refractory orthostatic hypotension, active gastrointestinal bleeding, or acquired factor X deficiency with active bleeding. Conditioning melphalan should be dose-adjusted (200 mg/m² or 140 mg/m²) according to age, cardiac status, renal function, and overall condition
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lenalidomide and the newer proteasome inhibitors (carfilzomib, ixazomib) have a limited role,** alone or combined, because of cardiotoxicity risk and little evidence of efficacy. Fibril-directed antibodies (birtamimab, anselamimab) failed their phase 3 trials.
claims.source_text: Use of immunomodulatory drugs, such as lenalidomide, or proteasome inhibitors (e.g., carfilzomib, ixazomib) alone or in combination is limited, due to the increased potential for cardiotoxicity and lack of evidence of efficacy … Although Phase 3 studies have been conducted for anti-amyloid agents such as birtamimab and anselamimab, these trials did not meet their primary endpoints
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Relapse:** consider daratumumab rechallenge, or a daratumumab-based regimen if not used before; bortezomib re-exposure (ideally in a different combination) if the earlier response was durable and there is no neuropathy; venetoclax (investigational) for t(11;14); and clinical trials.
claims.source_text: Regarding second-line treatment, daratumumab rechallenge can be considered, with bortezomib re-exposure also being an option in certain circumstances. Patients who achieve a durable, well-tolerated response to a bortezomib-containing regimen, particularly in the absence of neuropathy, may be considered for proteasome inhibitor re-exposure, ideally employing a different combination. For patients who have not previously received anti-CD38 therapy, daratumumab-based regimens represent a reasonable option []. Also, enrollment in clinical trials should be encouraged if feasible … While not currently FDA approved, venetoclax is an investigational second-line treatment option for patients with AL amyloidosis with the t(11;14) translocation
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Measure haematological response as dFLC (involved minus uninvolved free light chain) at least every three months** during and after treatment; reaching dFLC below 10 mg/L predicts better survival and organ response.
claims.source_text: Hematological response is measured as the difference between involved and uninvolved free light chains (dFLC) [,] and organ response is assessed by measuring organ-specific biomarkers … achieving a dFLC < 10 mg/L predicts superior overall survival, higher organ response rates, and a longer time to next treatment [,]. Assessment of hematological response should be conducted at least every three months while on active treatment and after completion of treatment; proper monitoring should begin early, especially in the initial treatment phase
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rising dFLC does not automatically mean second-line therapy;** individualise. After a prior very good partial response (dFLC under 40 mg/L), consider salvage before overt organ progression. High-risk dFLC progression means dFLC over 20 mg/L (over 20% of baseline) and a more than 50% rise from the nadir.
claims.source_text: As rising dFLC levels per se do not uniformly mandate the initiation of second-line therapy, an individualized approach is needed … in patients who previously achieved a very good partial response defined as the dFLC < 40 mg/L or better, salvage therapy should be considered in the presence of rising dFLC levels before overt organ progression develops, even if hematologic progression is not seen … This is best captured by the concept of 'high-risk dFLC progression' (dFLC > 20 mg/L, representing > 20% of the baseline and a > 50% increase from the nadir)
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not mistake localised AL (about 10% of cases) for systemic disease:** there is no circulating monoclonal protein or organ involvement, it rarely becomes systemic, and chemotherapy is not indicated. Treat for symptoms with surgery first, radiotherapy if unresectable, or watch and wait.
claims.source_text: Localized AL amyloidosis accounts for around 10% of all amyloidosis cases []. In the clinical practice, localized AL amyloidosis may be misdiagnosed as systemic AL amyloidosis, leading to chemotherapy treatment that is not clinically indicated … In localized AL amyloidosis, there is typically no evidence of a circulating monoclonal protein or systemic organ involvement … Surgical resection is the most common first-line treatment [,], while radiotherapy can stabilize refractory and locally advanced disease that is not suitable for surgery. In some cases, a watch and wait strategy may be appropriate. Localized AL amyloidosis usually does not progress to systemic AL amyloidosis
claims.locator: Brazilian expert panel, Hematology, Transfusion and Cell Therapy, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of light chain amyloidosis', Jul–Sep 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13251756/, retrieved 2026-09-23
